title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
mutable_substrate: User-marked evolve blocks spanning an entire source file (up to hundreds of lines, in multiple programming languages), plus optionally a separately co-evolved meta-prompt database; applications evolve algorithms, constructors, search heuristics, Verilog RTL, or compiler IR.
optimization_operator: Gemini 2.0 Flash and Gemini 2.0 Pro generate semantic SEARCH/REPLACE diffs or full rewrites, conditioned on a parent program, sampled inspirations, rich domain context, and rendered evaluation feedback; the mutations are accumulated through an evolutionary loop.
feedback_selection: A user-provided evaluate function returns one or more scalar scores to maximize. Evaluation cascades prune weak candidates, multiobjective scores promote diversity, and an evolutionary database inspired by MAP-Elites and island populations balances exploration and exploitation.
archive_memory: A persistent program database stores every candidate with scores and execution outputs and resamples promising or behaviorally diverse programs as parents and inspirations; meta-prompts can be maintained in a separate analogous database. Exact database rules are not disclosed.
validation_strategy: Task-specific executable evaluation, staged test cascades, repeated randomized seeds, exact integer/half-integer reconstruction for tensor decompositions, released mathematical certificates and verification code, held-out workloads or input shapes for production heuristics, randomized differential testing, correctness-preserving interfaces, and final human expert review for deployed hardware/compiler changes.
adaptation_mode: Offline asynchronous population evolution with parallel candidate generation and evaluation, followed by selection and, for production cases, held-out validation and human-gated deployment. The deployed Borg heuristic acts online, but the evolutionary adaptation itself is not online continual learning.
benchmarks: More than 50 constructive mathematics problems across analysis, combinatorics, number theory, geometry, and packing
Google Borg fleet scheduling simulator and unseen recent fleet workloads
Gemini Pallas matrix-multiplication kernel shapes on real TPU accelerators
XLA-generated FlashAttention IR for a high-impact GPU inference configuration
principal_results: Across 54 matrix-multiplication targets, surpasses the known rank in 14 cases, matches 38, and trails 2.
Finds a rank-48 tensor decomposition for 4x4 complex-valued matrix multiplication, the first characteristic-zero improvement over recursive Strassen rank 49 in 56 years.
Across more than 50 constructive mathematics problems, matches best-known constructions in about 75% and improves the state of the art in about 20%.
Raises the dimension-11 kissing-number lower bound from 592 to 593 with a verifiable integral-coordinate construction.
A deployed Borg scheduling heuristic recovers an average 0.7% of otherwise stranded fleet-wide compute.
A deployed Pallas tiling heuristic yields a 23% average kernel speedup and a 1% reduction in overall Gemini training time, reducing optimization work from months to days.
A verified Verilog rewrite removes unnecessary bits from a TPU arithmetic circuit and is integrated into an upcoming TPU, though downstream synthesis independently found the same improvement.
Optimized XLA IR speeds a FlashAttention kernel by 32% and its pre/postprocessing by 15%.
limitations: Requires a trustworthy automated evaluator; tasks dependent on manual experiments remain out of scope.
Full implementation, proprietary evaluators, population-database rules, prompt details, and absolute compute/token/cost budgets are not released.
A candidate evaluation can consume on the order of 100 compute-hours, and larger tensor targets can exhaust single-GPU memory across 1,000 seeds.
Two of 54 tensor targets trail known ranks; one improved rank was concurrently discovered; one TPU edit was also found by synthesis tools.
The uncertainty appendix documents initially missing stronger prior art before a revised method produced a new bound.
LLM-based qualitative scoring is less grounded than executable metrics and is not the system's optimized regime.
No general security threat model or generated-code sandbox design is reported.
safety_controls: Explicit source markers constrain mutable regions.
Evaluation cascades reject faulty or weak programs before expensive tests.
Borg candidates rank only machines already declared feasible by the production scheduler.
Held-out workload and kernel-shape sets test generalization before release.
Randomized differential tests compare compiler IR candidates with reference behavior.
Exact reconstruction and mathematical certificates guard against numerical false positives.
TPU designers and compiler experts review final deployment candidates.

explicit_predecessors.name: FunSearch
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper calls AlphaEvolve a substantial enhancement of FunSearch and explicitly contrasts single-function Python evolution and one fast metric with full-file, multi-language, multiobjective evolution using rich context, frontier LLMs, and expensive parallel evaluation.

explicit_predecessors.name: Classical evolutionary and genetic programming
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The related-work section places AlphaEvolve in the mutation-selection population tradition while identifying LLM-generated semantic code edits as a replacement for handwritten mutation and crossover operators.

explicit_predecessors.name: MAP-Elites and island population models
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The evolution section states that the program database is inspired by a combination of MAP-Elites and island-based population models to balance quality, diversity, exploration, and exploitation.

explicit_predecessors.name: AlphaTensor
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper identifies prior specialized reinforcement-learning work on matrix-multiplication tensor decomposition and contrasts it with AlphaEvolve's general-purpose code-evolution approach.

explicit_predecessors.name: Program superoptimization
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper explicitly interprets AlphaEvolve as code superoptimization driven by iterative execution feedback, extending enumerative, genetic, stochastic, and reinforcement-learning approaches with an LLM mutation operator.

open_questions: How do evolutionary memory, base-model capability, prompt context, and evaluator compute contribute under equal absolute cost?
Can the program database's sampling, niching, migration, retention, and replacement rules be fully specified and independently reproduced?
What standardized held-out selection protocol best prevents evaluator overfitting across scientific and production tasks?
Can formal verification replace randomized or expert-only validation for source, compiler, and hardware transformations?
How should a practitioner choose among direct-object, constructor, search-program, and co-evolution representations?
Can evolutionary trajectories be distilled into base models without losing long-horizon improvement capability?
What sandboxing and anti-reward-hacking controls are required for long-running generated-code evolution?
How can subjective hypothesis evaluation be safely connected to an execution-grounded implementation phase?
